entry.guide_markdown:
## Trumbull County, Ohio — Locality Research Guide (1954–1975)

### Jurisdiction
- **Trumbull County** was organized 10 July 1800 from Jefferson and Wayne counties. County seat: Warren.
- No boundary changes during the target period; Trumbull County is the sole jurisdiction.
- A courthouse fire in **1895** damaged some earlier records; the 1954–1975 window is unaffected.

### Marriage Records — Excellent Coverage
The primary source is **Ohio, County Marriages, 1789–2016** (FS collection 1614804) — index & images. All Trumbull County marriage volumes for 1950–1975 (Volumes 47–105) are **100% name-indexed and full-text searchable** on FamilySearch. Each record can supply: full names of bride and groom, ages, dates of birth, place of residence, place of birth, occupations, and names of fathers and mothers.

- Marriage licenses and certificates have been combined since 1891.
- Physical access: Trumbull County Archives (185 E. Market St., Warren, OH; 330-675-6615) holds an alphabetical card index plus original certificates.
- Also on MyHeritage: Ohio Marriages (1789–onward, $).
- Ohio, Marriages, 1800–1958 (FS 1681001) is index-only and covers through 1958 only.

### Browse-Only County Court Records
**Ohio, Trumbull County Records, 1795–2010** (FS 2065327) — **0% indexed, browse-only images** (788,995 images). Navigate the waypoints: Record Category → Record Type → Volume/Year. Contains additional marriage and naturalization documents not in the indexed collection.

### Census Records
- 1950 US Census: Available on FamilySearch (multiple Trumbull County ED volumes, ~87–98% indexed).
- 1960 Census: Not publicly available until 2032 (72-year rule).

### Death Records
- Ohio, County Death Records, 1840–2001 (FS 2128172) — index & images.
- Ohio, Death Index, 1908–2007 (FS 1949341) — index only for 1958–2007 window.
- Death certificates from 1954+ are held by the Ohio Department of Health.
- Ohio, Deaths, 1908–1953 (FS 1307272) — for deaths through 1953 only.
- Social Security Death Index (FS 1202535) — useful for post-1935 deaths.

### Church Records
- Ohio, Church Records, 1762–2008 (FS 2787827) — index & images; denominational coverage varies.
- Italian-Catholic community records may be held at individual parishes; the Diocese of Youngstown (encompassing Trumbull County) was established 1943.

### Newspapers
- Warren Tribune Chronicle obituary index at Warren-Trumbull County Public Library (1900–1949).
- Ohio Newspapers, 1793–2009 (MyHeritage, $); Ohio History Connection digitized newspapers.
- Ancestry Newspapers.com covers Ohio through the 1970s ($).

### Physical Repositories
- **Trumbull County Records Center & Archives**, 185 E Market St, Warren, OH 44481; 330-675-6615 — marriage, birth, probate.
- **Trumbull County Courthouse** (Probate Judge) — marriage licenses and probate records.
- **Warren-Trumbull County Public Library** — FamilySearch affiliate library; genealogy resources.

### External Links
- Ancestry Ohio County Marriage Records, 1774–1993 (collection 61378)
- Ancestry Ohio Marriage Abstracts, 1970–2022 (collection 2025)
- MyHeritage Ohio Marriages, 1970–2003 (collection 10212)
- Ohio Genealogical Society (ogs.org) — obituary and other indexes ($)

entry.rationale: Ohio, County Marriages, 1789-2016 (FS 1614804) is the primary indexed source for Trumbull County marriage licenses. Per loc_001, all volumes for 1950-1975 are 100% name-indexed and full-text searchable. A marriage license will supply both spouses' full names, ages, dates of birth, parents' names, residence, and marriage date and place — direct evidence answering the question. Amelia born 1936; marriage window ~1954-1975 based on her age and 2014 death.

Amelia Frances Gioiello died 1 Aug 2014 in Cortland, Trumbull County, Ohio. Her Ohio death certificate (FS Ohio County Death Records 1840-2001, collection 2128172, or Ohio Death Index 1908-2007, collection 1949341) will name the informant — typically a surviving spouse or child — and may list her marital status and surviving spouse's name. This is strong indirect evidence of the spouse's identity even if the marriage record itself is not yet found.

Amelia was buried in Cortland, Trumbull County, Ohio in 2014 (per tree.gedcomx.json). A Find A Grave or BillionGraves memorial for her burial site frequently names a co-interred or surviving spouse and lists family relationships. This is a freely accessible secondary source that can quickly identify or corroborate the spouse's name before or alongside the vital record search.

An obituary published in the Warren Tribune Chronicle or a Niles-area paper at Amelia's death (Aug 2014) would name her husband (or widower), children, and surviving family. Trumbull County newspapers are accessible via the Warren-Trumbull County Public Library obituary index, GenealogyBank, and Ancestry/Newspapers.com. The obituary is a strong secondary source for spouse identity and marriage context.

If the FamilySearch indexed search (pli_001) returns no result due to indexing variants of 'Gioiello' (e.g., Gioello, Joiello, Gioyello) or a marriage outside the primary index window, Ancestry's Ohio County Marriage Records, 1774-1993 (collection 61378) and Ohio Marriage Abstracts, 1970-2022 (collection 2025) provide an independent index against which to cross-check. Ancestry's search engine handles spelling variants differently and may surface records missed by FS.

Ohio, Trumbull County Records, 1795-2010 (FS 2065327) is 0% name-indexed and browse-only (788,995 images). Per loc_001, navigate via waypoints: Record Category > Marriages > Volume/Year. If the indexed FS and Ancestry searches (pli_001, pli_005) both fail — possible if the bride was indexed under a badly garbled name variant — the original marriage register pages can be browsed volume by volume for the relevant year range. Use the marriage date narrowed by other sources to target the correct volume.
